docs.purpose: One page listing every screen, every API contract and every scheduled job in the product, generated directly from the declarations that define them. It answers 'what does this system actually consist of, and which parts is anyone using' — including a seven-day usage count beside each entry. Because the page is generated rather than hand-written, it cannot quietly fall out of date: if a declaration is missing or wrong, the page is visibly empty or visibly wrong.
docs.data_story: Nothing is built yet, so nothing is measured here. As specified it would read `usage_events` — of which `usage_events` does **not exist yet** and must be declared, migrated and drift-asserted before this page can render a single row.
docs.under_126: **NEW.** It does not exist; it is generated from descriptors from its first commit, through the LIST renderer (a collection with declared pagination, recycling and empty/offline states). It is **100% generated** — which is the point: if the descriptor set is incomplete or an archetype profile is wrong, this page is visibly empty or visibly wrong on commit 1, and cannot be faked by hand.

rls_class.why: Spec 114 §2 is definitional: everything that is not one of the 10 named Class-A tables, not profiles and not Class D is Class B by default, including tables added after that spec was written — which covers surface_descriptors, contract_descriptors and archetype_registry. Class B is ENABLE ROW LEVEL SECURITY with zero policies, and per Spec 114 §4 / D1 the Next.js admin route connects as the table owner, so it is outside RLS enforcement entirely.
evidence: docs/specs/00-architecture/114_rls_policy_catalog.md §2 — "everything else is Class B by default — including tables added after this spec is written"
docs/specs/00-architecture/114_rls_policy_catalog.md §4 — Class B is one ENABLE statement and no CREATE POLICY; admin/pipeline connections are RLS-exempt as table owner (Decision D1)

checks.why: Every row it renders is a descriptor; a descriptor that no longer parses against the generated Zod mirror must render as schema_drift, not vanish from the list.
The filter axes are part of the key; a key built from an object literal would refetch the whole registry on every render.
The LIST profile requires it, and it is the pilot's whole point: an incomplete descriptor set must render as a visibly empty page on commit 1 rather than as a plausible one.
Each declared error class renders its declared UI; a 500 must not read as "no surfaces exist".
R-13 totality is the registry's own load-bearing claim — a component owned by two surfaces or by none makes the ownership column fiction, so it gates the render.
Spec 128 rule 14: every declared column of the three seeded tables is asserted against the live catalog both directions before the page renders a row from them.
Permanently non-zero until usage_events has a live writer: the usage column renders "not_yet_metered", never a zero, and the retighten condition is the first metered contract landing.

R-18: the surface says admin, so every contract it lists itself as calling must declare auth_class admin — the /builders-gated vs /api/builders-public mismatch is the measured reason this check exists.

invariants.sql: SELECT count(*) FROM surface_descriptors WHERE git_sha IS NULL OR descriptor IS NULL
invariants.why: LM-D15 applied to surfaces: a seeded row with no git_sha or no descriptor payload is a half-applied seed, and the deploy gate must throw rather than render it.

invariants.sql: SELECT count(*) FROM surface_descriptors s WHERE NOT EXISTS (SELECT 1 FROM archetype_registry a WHERE a.archetype = s.archetype)
invariants.why: Spec 126 §3.5 unknown-archetype posture: a surface whose archetype has no registry row has no renderer, and must be a red row rather than a blank cell.

plausibility.why: The estate is 53 rendering surfaces + 6 shells (Spec 126 §3.1); a seeded count far outside [40, 80] means the seed ran against the wrong tree, which a count nobody looks at would hide.

limitations.what: The LIST required-field profile in Spec 126 §3.1 mandates list.item_archetype, list.pagination and list.recycling, and surface.schema.json has no property for any of them (the top level and every category are additionalProperties:false).
limitations.measured: Every allOf block in scripts/surfaces/_schema/surface.schema.json is `"then": true` — the archetype profiles are declared in prose in Spec 126 §3.1 and enforced by nothing, so these fields cannot be declared here and are not caught missing either.

limitations.what: The usage_7d column cannot show a real number until usage_events exists and has a live writer.
limitations.measured: Spec 126 §7: there is no working meter to extend — /api/leads/view is the repo's only one and it has no caller. The column therefore renders "not_yet_metered", never 0.

notes: Report §1.1 row 17 and §5 — the RECOMMENDED PILOT surface, to land at /admin/surfaces. Its other inputs are the SURFACE + CONTRACT + JOB descriptor files, which are not DB tables and do not exist in the tree yet (VERIFIED: no surfaces/, contracts/ or jobs/ directory at the repo root). Measured defect it makes visible: the census headline finding, /api/leads/view — a live metered route with zero production callers — would have been a red row on day one instead of months of silence. Per AQ9 the usage column renders 'not_yet_metered' until usage_events exists, never a zero. DESIGNED, NOT MEASURED — every category on this row is a design choice grounded in a spec §, not an observation of code. THREE DECISIONS THIS ROW COULD NOT TAKE: (1) `status` — the task asked for `status: "designed"`, which is not in the closed set {exists, new, generated} (surface.schema.json properties.status; generate-surface-registry.mjs:182 refuses anything else). Per the research brief §4 rule 1 a value the menu lacks is an escalation, never a per-row invention, so the row keeps `new` ("Specified, not built. Nothing is measured.") and the gap is filed here. (2) `inputs.contract_ref` is EMPTY although the surface calls a designed contract: generate-surface-registry.mjs:195 refuses a contract_ref entry that is neither a census contract path nor a census id, so the designed `GET /api/admin/surfaces` is recorded in evidence.contracts instead. A designed surface therefore renders as a zero-out-degree node in the very fan-out graph this estate is building. (3) `identity.route` is set only because Spec 126 §2.2.2 fixes /admin/surfaces by name.
